name: glm-redsnow-tp2-mtp
_comment: Portable configuration example: host, user and private workspace paths are placeholders, not original measured infrastructure. Historical context follows; this is not a new qualification claim. The RED-SNOW 4.91bpw GLM-5.3-Flash pack as a two-rank group WITH NextN (MTP) speculation (lane L12, docs/GLM_TP.md section 9; the text-only group is lane L9's cluster.glm-redsnow-tp2.json): N1 = rank 0, N4 = rank 1, each mapping and allocating only its share of the routed experts, the NextN layer's included (its layer 45 is uniform 4/4/4: one subbank of 144 experts a rank, 1.69 GiB). --spec auto on rank 0; tools/glm_tp_mtp_two_node.sh derives the --spec none (serial) leg. Its MTP head is quantized at 4 bits and its text side is fine-tuned: the gate is drafted == serial, acceptance is measured and recorded. N2 and N3 are the gn100s: disabled by owner rule.

memory._comment: the rank planner on the pack's header (CPU): a rank's regions 96.45 GiB (rank 0) / 96.42 GiB (rank 1) with the NextN layer (94.61 / 94.59 without: +1.83 GiB), KV 13,056 B per token with the drafter's cache; these flags (2 slots, 16,384 KV tokens) need 110.25 GiB free (108.4 without the layer); the restricted draft head (about 0.23 GiB) comes on top, out of the planner's headroom. About 13.5 GiB stay available on a 117 GiB node while the group runs: under the box's 20 GiB rule, stated here rather than hidden
